question: Should crawl-remote deployments permanently retain the hidden Gitcrawl canary across Worker rollback and require predecessor runtimes to advertise canary and per-query release-provenance support?
rationale: Tests can verify implementation consistency, but they cannot decide whether permanent production seed data and a fail-closed predecessor-runtime requirement are the intended long-term deployment and rollback contract.

options.title: Approve permanent canary
options.body: Accept the retained hidden rows and predecessor-runtime gate, then sequence the two prerequisite PRs before this branch lands.

options.title: Require lifecycle cleanup
options.body: Revise the design to include a maintainer-approved canary migration, replacement, or cleanup contract before merge.

options.title: Defer deployment hardening
options.body: Pause this stacked branch until the broader Gitcrawl evidence architecture and rollout policy are settled.

recommendation.title: Approve permanent canary
recommendation.body: Accept the retained hidden rows and predecessor-runtime gate, then sequence the two prerequisite PRs before this branch lands.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest available technical owner across the six-query, deployment-canary, and evidence-receipt stack and can explain the intended rollback contract.
